---
title: "Some guidelines for statistical writing"
---

# Avoid "AI tropes"

These "tropes" are not how we talk to each other or write about our work naturally. When I see them, it signals AI use. 

- "It's not X -- it's Y"
- "Not X. Not Y. Just Z."
- "The X? A Y."
- Em-dash overuse
- Short punchy fragments of sentences
- Repeating the same sentence opening multiple times
- Bold text/bullet points combinations
- Overstating results; lack of uncertainty
- Characters that can't be typed directly on a keyboard
- Stating something is obvious, clear, or simple instead of proving it or providing justification
- Listicle in a trench coat
- "The same point, restated eight ways across 4000 words"
- Inflating the stakes
- Magic adverbs: "quietly", "deeply", "fundamentally"
- Teacher-student dynamic ("let's break this down", "let's unpack this", ...)
- Signposting conclusions 
- Inventing labels
